slides.texte_overlay:
hobbies that will make you
dangerously confident

saying i don't know

say "i don't know" out loud the next time you don't, instead of nodding along. people trust you more once they've heard you admit it, and you stop living in fear of being found out.

one clean apology

when you're wrong, apologise once, clearly, without ten excuses. a short real apology shows strength, and a long nervous one only shows how afraid you are of being judged.

asking directly

for a week, ask for exactly what you want instead of hinting: the window seat, more time, a day off. hints make people guess, and guessing makes them say no.

no more nodding along

spend 5 minutes a day on something you've always pretended to understand: the stock market, black holes, a famous book. knowing it for real is quieter than faking it, and it shows.
slides.texte_sophia:
no more nodding along

spend 5 minutes a day on something you've always pretended to understand: the stock market, black holes. a micro-learning app like the Sophia app makes it easy, and you can stop nodding along.

slides.texte_overlay:
laughing at yourself first

when you trip, spill or say something wrong, laugh at it first. people who can laugh at themselves are impossible to embarrass, and everyone around them relaxes.
